questions.prompt: Explain why a small increase in a vehicle’s speed makes crashes much more dangerous.
questions.modelAnswer: Kinetic energy depends on the square of speed (KE = ½mv²). A small increase in speed causes a much bigger increase in kinetic energy; for example doubling the speed gives four times the energy. In a crash all this energy must be transferred (to bending metal, heat and injuries), and a longer braking distance is needed to remove it, so the damage is much greater.
rubric: Small speed increase gives large KE increase
More energy to remove: longer stopping distance and more damage
